rationale: Start with Astra: the source changes to v2 while the cache and agent still hold v1, making the cost of a stale tool result visible before showing explicit recovery. Baseline is the simpler introduction to misses, hits and expiry; Fable is the stronger follow-on for reproducing a delayed refill that defeats deletion. Astra offers the clearest first viewing at phone size, while Fable’s overlapping reader and writer reward a pause or replay.
findings: Baseline 00:00.6–00:06.6 and 00:08.6–00:11.5 makes application-owned fetch/fill and database avoidance easiest to trace. Its revised TTL bar drains from insertion through the hit to expiry at 00:14.5, but no source write occurs, so this cut alone cannot teach freshness.

Astra 00:06.4–00:11.8 leaves v1 visible in the cache and agent after the source becomes v2. Its large version fields and HIT ≠ FRESH conclusion communicate the chapter’s central warning more directly than Baseline’s envelopes or Fable’s smaller policy rows.

Astra 00:14.1–00:23.35 shows explicit deletion, a subsequent miss, source read, cache fill and delivery in that order. The agent retains its old result until the new response arrives; deletion does not repair already-returned data. The editor and recovery trigger are abstracted, and this serialized success is not a concurrency guarantee.

Fable 00:10.2–00:13.6 holds SET 14d while a writer commits 7d and deletes the empty key, then lets the old fill land. This concrete race is absent from the other cuts and directly supports the guide’s paused-reader exercise. Enlarged values and feedback beside the row fix the original phone-legibility and value-overlap weaknesses.

Fable 00:15–00:22.94 shows two stale hits without renewing the entry’s TTL, then expiration. This reinforces persistence but makes the 31.57-second cut denser than Astra; 30d/14d/7d are policy values, and the clock limits this cache entry after its late insertion, not the age of source data.

Baseline delivers its final response at 00:22, Astra at 00:28.25, and Fable at 00:27.67. All leave a readable outcome before fading and have pixel-identical first/last decoded frames; Baseline and Fable retain their titles, while Astra returns to an empty dark frame.
contentVerdict: Keep as reference. Exact-key caching becomes useful when repeated tool retrieval creates measured source load or latency; it is not a prerequisite for adopting agents. The guide earns its place through an observable stale-fill exercise, explicit freshness and authorization boundaries, and source-load controls. Preserve the existing reference classification; establish trustworthy tool contracts and review boundaries before optimizing retrieval.
defectsFixed: Baseline: added a topic title and caller/TTL labels; made the lifetime bar drain continuously from each fill without hit renewal; rerendered and regenerated the poster.
Baseline: used the topic-local normalized encoder with deterministic loop endpoints and at most two FFmpeg encoder/filter threads; preserved unknown original model provenance.

Fable: moved hit/miss/expiry feedback off the policy value; enlarged row, source, badge and packet text; renamed the subtitle STALE FILL RACE; rerendered and regenerated the poster without changing causal timing.
Fable: corrected overly broad TTL claims in lesson metadata, scene commentary, README and beat sheet; clarified policy values versus lifetime and the persistent closing title in its transcript.

Guide: distinguished EXPIRE’s timeout-setting from later deletion, aligned exercise steps and source-fetch counts, added the primary stale-set paper, and separated a revision check from enforcement at action execution.
Both edited cuts retain original provenance plus editedBy and corrections metadata. Original sources, author reviews and pre-edit hashes are preserved in the comparison folder.
limitations: Audio was analysed using full decode, sample peaks, cue-window energy and spectrograms; it was not heard. Energy during overlapping cue windows does not prove each cue is individually audible or comfortable.

Visual review used decoded half-second contact sheets across each complete duration, exact full-size and 350px beat/busy/ending frames, and exact endpoints; it was not an uninterrupted real-time viewing of every frame.
No real cache service, deployment, concurrency implementation or team exercise was executed. Timing is illustrative and no latency, freshness, authorization or capacity guarantee is measured.

Fable’s simultaneous operations and short write/delete transitions remain more demanding on first viewing. The second stale hit is retained as useful reinforcement; the transcript supports pausing or replay.
Primary-source claims were checked in the relevant sections listed in content-review.md, not every page of every source. Astra’s source, metadata and media remain unchanged.
This is a topic-scoped comparison, not a release or publication. Other concepts and shared build/app files were not modified.
